correctness.rationale: The explicit Fourier transform of both Poisson kernels gives a positive bounded two-step Jacobi matrix and exact Gram identity. Weighted atomic Fourier vectors are dense, so positive definiteness is equivalent to the operator bound. The geometric-tail Schur test certifies every principal-section error. At zero secondary scale the top rank-one eigenpair gives the quadratic expansion; at equal scales a unique gapped odd-block defect eigenvalue gives the exact endpoint and localized near-endpoint Rayleigh slope, with an O((r-s)^2) remainder from the Schur complement. The boundary Fourier recurrence forces F_n->0 for s<r, contradicting the positive finite-atom Cesaro mean; at s=r uniqueness of the top bound state gives the antipodal signed null pair. value.rationale: Signed covariance subtraction is a natural admissibility problem; its sharp relative Fourier eigenvalue is an exact invariant, quantitatively certified by exponentially convergent finite sections. The first axial cosine and two Poisson semigroup scales are canonical rather than arbitrary slices. The result detects qualitative finite-site rigidity that is absent at the equal-scale endpoint, and gives nontrivial sharp quadratic/linear sensitivity coefficients. These are useful mathematical structure and numerical benchmarks not supplied by the generic positivity test alone.
